description: The Settings window (desktop refinement §14.1). It is granted the SAME application-command permission as the control window, and that is a deliberate decision rather than convenience: Settings is where the speech model is downloaded and verified, where displays are listed and identified, where the optical rigs are calibrated, where a backup is exported or restored, and where the support bundle is written. Narrowing the grant would mean maintaining a second list that has to be widened every time a setting gains a backing command — and a list that is wrong in the closed direction fails as a broken screen, which is the kind of failure people work around by widening it in a hurry. What this does NOT mean is that the window is bounded by having no library, editor or session UI: `allow-control-commands` includes listing and deleting scripts and starting and ending sessions, and a compromised renderer invokes commands directly rather than through buttons. The grant is as wide as control's, and it is accepted as such. What is genuinely withheld is what is withheld from control too — `opener:default` and the dialog plugin — so no window in this application can choose a filesystem path; every picker runs in Rust (§50.7).
